identifier: cal-pixel-size-20260919 -- the operator's own measurement of pixel size at the sample plane, for six objectives at both intermediate magnifications, at 1x1 binning, reported to this store on 2026-09-19.
grade_rule: E2 via a `calibration:` source, which 12 routes for a calibration the operator performed on this instrument, with a validity period AND a condition range both required rather than optional -- the period stands in for the traceability a result card would carry (rule 9, corrected 2026-09-19). Not E1: E1 needs a run_id from this system.
validity_period: fifteen years, stated by the operator. Anchored to 2026-09-19 because that is the date the store has; the day the measurements were taken was not recorded, so the anchor is the report and not the event.
condition: 1x1 binning, stated by the operator on 2026-09-19. It is the one condition of this calibration that is a quantity rather than a nominal designation, which is why it is the one that reaches `validity` -- the objective and the zoom are exact identifiers and live in `identifiers`.
license_note: The values are the operator's own; nothing is reproduced from elsewhere.
note: The operator confirmed, after being shown the arithmetic, that all twelve are direct measurements rather than one measurement scaled to the others. Each entry records both that confirmation and what the numbers relate by, because the second is a checkable property of the set and the next reader will find it whether or not it is written down.
standing_2026_09_21: THE OPERATOR RULED, ON 2026-09-21, THAT THIS CALIBRATION WILL NOT BE REPEATED AND THE TWELVE VALUES STAND AS THEY ARE. Asked what event ends them before the stated fifteen years, the operator settled two of the four candidates the store implies. (1) NO RECALIBRATION IS PLANNED -- so the event that would most obviously supersede these is ruled out rather than merely unscheduled. (2) A CHANGE OF OBJECTIVE DOES NOT END ANY OF THEM: the operator's words were that using a different objective means reading a different row. That confirms from the operator's side what the entries already imply structurally -- each row carries its objective and intermediate magnification in `identifiers`, exact by definition, so an objective change SELECTS among the twelve rather than invalidating one.
what_the_2026_09_21_ruling_did_not_settl: Two of the four candidates, and they are left open rather than closed by silence. A CAMERA CHANGE would end all twelve at once -- pixel size at the sample plane is the sensor pitch over the magnification, camera_sensor_geometry carries the Kinetix22's 6.5 um pitch, and that entry itself carries no valid_until. A CHANGE IN THE OPTICS BETWEEN OBJECTIVE AND CAMERA would do the same and the store holds nothing about that path at all. Neither was put to the operator, so neither is entered. `valid_until` on the twelve therefore still carries a bare date and no `event`, and that is now a recorded state rather than an omission: what is missing is not the operator's answer but a question nobody has asked yet.
why_this_is_here_and_not_only_in_an_entr: kb_version is a content hash over kb/entries/ alone -- measured on 2026-09-21 by rebuilding the index over a copy of kb/ with this file edited (version unchanged) and then with one entry edited (version moved). So a source record can take a ruling while a fan-out is mid-flight and an entry cannot. mic-20260920-001:v2 was pinned at kbv-e8f4a5610aa6 with its a6 axis still calling, so the ruling landed here first and the entries that make it reachable through kb_query follow once that fan-out closes. This is also where 024's record says the next person sourcing a quantity will look.
resolves_an_apparent_conflict: objective_change_invalidates_trap_calibration (E3, transferred from the prior project) claims that changing the objective silently invalidates a pixel-to-micrometre calibration. That is about the optical tweezers' GUI and not about these twelve, and without this ruling a reader meeting both has no way to tell which applies where. The difference is that the tweezers hold ONE calibration that an objective change falsifies, and this calibration holds TWELVE rows indexed BY objective.
contradicted_2026_09_24: A WRITTEN RECORD FROM THE PRIOR PROJECT CONTRADICTS THE OPERATOR'S CONFIRMATION, AND IT IS UNRESOLVED. C:/agentic_microscope/config/micromanager/single_cam_red_noDMD_nocom10.cfg (sha256 8184073e31e1a7a63731932a20a622131d4dba04cf839bc9e651bf9abcd53120), in the comment above its PixelSize block (lines 278-296 as read 2026-09-24), says its values come from 'Confocal_microscope_conversion_factor(Apr 2025).xlsx' at Kinetix binning 1 and that 'Only 20x is a measurement. The other five are exactly 6.5/M to every digit they carry'. Its six 1x values equal the six 1x entries here to every digit, so it is very likely the same numbers and corroborates nothing. RECOMPUTED HERE, NOT TAKEN FROM THE FILE: 4x 1.625, 10x 0.65, 40x 0.1625, 60x 0.10833 and 100x 0.065 are exactly 6.5 um / M, and 20x 0.32373 is not (6.5/20 = 0.325). The file does not mention a second thing, which this record's own note already implies: all six 1.5x rows equal the 1x row divided by 1.5, to every digit they carry, 20x included (0.32373/1.5 = 0.21582). So on the file's account one of the twelve is a measurement, and the other eleven are arithmetic. RULING ON THE ITEM: recorded as a disagreement only. No value, date or grade crosses from the prior project. It is capped at E3 and it does not outrank the operator's statement, which is this calibration's E2 basis. The twelve entries are not regraded on it. That waits for the person, who has been asked whether they confirm the operator's account. If the file is right, eleven rows are E4-shaped arithmetic from one measurement and 6.5 um, and the one measurement is 20x at 1x. THE DATE: the file names April 2025 as the spreadsheet's date, which is the first evidence of when the measurement happened. It is a filename in a prior-project comment, so it is not entered as the measurement date either. Reported by manager-microscope-20260924-1. Today's run uses only the 20x-at-1x value, which both accounts call a measurement.
